checks.finding: 2025 global PV LCOE 44 USD/MWh, onshore wind 33 USD/MWh, installed PV 667 USD/kW and installed four-hour BESS 140 USD/kWh confirmed. Report uses 2025 USD. Its historical series revises the older extract supplied in the sourcebook.
Figure 9.2 identifies 2010–2015 installed BESS values as calculated from Schmidt/Staffell regression data. The 2010 sourcebook anchor is a published reconstruction, not an observed procurement price.

Table 1 confirms Nevada 113.2 USD/MWh at 95% annual-energy coverage versus 43.5 USD/MWh PV baseline. Figure 10 gives 163/113/77/59 USD/MWh for 2020/2025/2030/2035. Hourly optimisation of a flat annual load; not a count of fully served hours or guaranteed firm supply.

Page 8 confirms gas 48–109, coal 71–173 and nuclear 141–220 USD/MWh. Coal and nuclear reuse inflation-adjusted v14 estimates; nuclear uses then-estimated Vogtle costs. These are published US new-build estimates, not an observed global plant survey.

9 December 2025 release confirms all-use Li-ion packs 108 USD/kWh and stationary packs 70 USD/kWh. These are pack prices, not installed storage-system costs. Earlier pack values are retained from the supplied extract.

boundaries: Generation LCOE, module USD/W and battery USD/kWh capacity have different denominators.

Daily shifting is an author engineering scenario: 60% of delivered energy through storage, no seasonal or firm-supply guarantee. Installed capacity prices are treated as usable capacity as a simplifying assumption.
The global BESS benchmark is used in a generic Li-ion model; it is not a chemistry-specific observed LFP project LCOE.
IRENA global renewables and Lazard US conventional generation are different samples; backcasts and future scenarios are not observations.
The sourcebook uses approximate CPI-U rebasing to 2025 USD. Its historical extraction may differ from revised current provider series.
